parameters.name: cal_rslv_hold_us
parameters.description: A14-R01: newest coherent resolver frame (block start) may be this old, else the angle is withdrawn. The hold may add at most the angle error the observer already carries at the acceleration envelope (alpha/wn^2): extrapolating adds e_w*t + alpha*t^2/2 with the observer's peak speed lag e_w = alpha/(e*wn), equal at t = 1.09/wn = 580 us (wn = 2 pi 300 Hz), whatever alpha; 500 us adds 0.26 deg el at alpha = 2e4 rad/s^2. Floor: 2 carrier periods + IRQ jitter (a normal empty read); ceiling: the observer's 8-block re-acquisition gap

parameters.name: cal_rslv_exc_target_vpp
parameters.description: A14-N01: SWG trim setpoint at the MONITOR plane (protected node, after RSX, before the PTC): amplifier 7.64 V pp (slew ceiling 8.28), SWG 1.84 V pp (low corner 1.884), winding 6.94 V pp cold

parameters.name: cal_rslv_wind_per_mon
parameters.description: A14-N01: downstream-loss allowance monitor -> winding, 70/(70 + 2 x 1.3) with the PTCs cold; the post-trip 5 ohm (70/80 = 0.875) is NOT credited: FW-10 flags it. EOL with the real harness replaces it

parameters.name: cal_swg_code_init
parameters.description: A14-N01: the SWG starts low (1.45 V pp at the MAXAPP max corner, IOAMPL assumed linear from MINAPP = 0.209 MAXAPP: silicon checklist, docs/target-bringup.md) and ramps up under the trim; <= 12 keeps the untrimmed max corner (1.94 V pp -> 8.0 V pp) under the slew ceiling

parameters.name: cal_sd_irq_lat_max_us
parameters.description: A16-R02 (round 18): a resolver block's first SDADC completion interrupt is serviced within this of the block's end, else the frame is not published and the ring re-acquires (a later one cannot tell a delay from a lap of the 4-slot ring). The priority-1 handler waits at most for the fault ISR (<= 10 us budget), a PRIMASK section and its two sibling handlers (~1 us each): ~13 us, x2.3 margin; floor 5 us above entry + the siblings; ceiling 45 us < half the 100 us carrier period. Round 19: the block's end is on the SWG-start cadence, so the SDADC's own output latency (decimation filter, FIFO watermark, eDMA) counts in it too — T-40 measures the sum from the carrier boundary

parameters.name: cal_swg_start_lat_us
parameters.description: A17-R01 (round 19): the resolver cadence's origin is the SWG start: hal_swg_start() anchors the ring at the later of two time reads around the enable, uncertain by the bracket (+1 us of timer resolution) plus this — the SGEN's start to its first period (the RM) plus the TRGMUX/SDADC trigger latency: sub-us each (a few bus/ADC clocks), 2 us allowed. It widens every completion window both ways and bounds every stamp's error (2 us + 1 = 3 us = 0.7 deg el at 10 000 rpm, 4 pole pairs); ceiling 20 us keeps the re-sync window (P/2 + 2 x uncertainty) inside the 100 us period. HIL-measured: T-42

parameters.name: cal_rslv_restart_max
parameters.description: A17-R01 (round 19): synchronized producer restarts per key cycle (a DMA out of phase with the carrier or lost samples: the rings re-armed, the SWG restarted and re-anchored, one DTC_RSLV_REACQUIRED each); then the resolver stays invalid for the key cycle (FW-28). 3: a transient and its repeat recover, a persistent fault stops the retries after three (the FW-28 age-out acts from the first loss); 0 = never restart

parameters.name: cal_ovs_warn_frac
parameters.description: FW-42 (round 23): the overspeed warning band starts at this fraction of the calibration record's n_max_rpm — the speed up to which the §6 release rules are proven (rule (a) at n_max, the ASC entry current, R8X-13): the §6 command-lost row (torque ramped to zero), the speed-limit request, no arming. Floor 0.90: a warning well before the maximum; ceiling 1.00: never beyond the proven envelope

parameters.name: cal_ovs_trip_frac
parameters.description: FW-42 (round 23): the overspeed trip band starts at this fraction of n_max_rpm: the §6 'control lost' row (SPO below n_x under the energy rule, LS-ASC at or above it), latched until a VCU fault reset below n_x. Floor 1.02: above every warning start (0.90–1.00), so the two bands never swap; ceiling 1.20: the release rules are evaluated at n_max, beyond it nothing is proven

parameters.name: cal_ovs_hyst_frac
parameters.description: FW-42 (round 23): each overspeed band is left this fraction of n_max_rpm below its start (320 rpm at 16 000 rpm): no chattering at a steady speed on a threshold

parameters.name: cal_ovs_debounce_ms
parameters.description: FW-42 (round 23): a band is entered or left only after this many consecutive 1 ms samples of the measured (resolver-valid) speed asking for it. The resolver's own plausibility (amplitude window, tracking error, acceleration — each debounced) rejects a corrupt frame; this bounds what remains, a speed-estimate transient of a few ms. 10 ms at the resolver acceleration bound (2e4 rad/s^2 el, 4 pole pairs: 48 000 rpm/s) is <= 480 rpm past a threshold

parameters.name: cal_rs_save_s
parameters.description: FW-43 (round 23): the run-time statistics record is queued at most this often while running, and once at controlled shutdown: the most an unclean shutdown loses, against data-flash wear (one ~100-byte record per period, Fee)

parameters.name: cal_isns_ofs_step_v
parameters.description: FW-44 (round 23): the tracked zero-current offset moves toward the key-on standstill mean by at most this per key cycle (2 mV = 0.9 A at 2.22 mV/A) — a slow track of the sensors' drift over life, never a jump; only when the mean passes the key-on check against the EOL offset (cal_isns_offset_tol_v, unchanged), so the tracked value stays inside that tolerance

parameters.name: cal_temp_rate_win_ms
parameters.description: FW-13 (round 23, item 1): the dT/dt plausibility compares the means of this window's 1 ms samples with the last accepted mean — over 1 ms one ADC code (0.04 degC at 50 degC, 0.5 degC at 125 degC) read 40-500 degC/s against cal_temp_rate_c_s; over 200 ms the bound is 4 degC; floor 100 ms (a code at 125 degC is then 5 degC/s), ceiling 250 ms (the derating value lags at most one window)

parameters.name: cal_temp_rate_db_codes
parameters.description: FW-13 (round 23, item 1): a window mean within this many ADC codes of the last accepted one never counts as a rate violation — ADC noise and quantization (+/-2 LSB on the SAR, below 1 code after the window's averaging) with margin

parameters.name: cal_ripple_ff_max_a
parameters.description: FW-46 (round 23): the torque-ripple feed-forward's authority — every table value is applied clamped to +/- this, and the tool's 0x2E FD46 write is refused (NRC 0x31) beyond it; 0 = the feed-forward off (the default: nothing is applied, bit for bit the image without it). Ceiling 30 A: the table's own range (int16, 0.01 A, calib_check), 23 N m of ripple on a 0.128 Wb, 4-pole-pair machine — cogging is a few % of the rated torque; T-58 sets it with the dyno's table

parameters.name: cal_ripple_ff_fmax_hz
parameters.description: FW-46 (round 23): the feed-forward is applied only while the cogging fundamental 6 f_e (six per electrical period, the three-phase machine's) is below this; above it the table is not applied at all. 200 Hz: 500 rpm at 4 pole pairs, where the loop (1.1 kHz crossover, 75 us actuation) still follows the table's 6th and 12th harmonics within 16 / 32 deg and the rotor's inertia already filters cogging; ceiling 500 Hz (half the SiC crossover); 0 = never

parameters.name: cal_temp_hold_ms
parameters.description: FW-13/FW-07/FW-09/FW-33 (round 24, F241): the slow list converts each of its inputs once per 1 ms task (hal_adc_start_slow; s32k396_cfg.h adc_slow_chain) and hal_adc_read returns the last conversion and its stamp until the next one. A sample whose stamp has not moved is HELD - the consumer's verdict kept, nothing counted again - while younger than this, then EXPIRED until a new conversion: a temperature channel invalid (FW-04's invalid-reading response), V5GD or VOFS leave V_DC invalid (the section-6 V_DC-invalid row), KL15, INTRLOK_N and VSUP read as never converted; DTC_ADC_SLOW_STALE. 10 ms = 10 periods: a late task or a lost conversion never expires it (floor 3 periods); ceiling 50 ms: an HVIL open during a stopped INTRLOK_N conversion is still seen within FW-09's 100 ms (50 + 3 x 10 ms)
